episodes.215261: The combination of abundant monsoonal moisture and an approaching easterly wave yielding repeated rounds of afternoon shower and thunderstorm activity over the South Fork burn scar near Ruidoso. Flash flooding was reported by local officials with multiple roads becoming impassible and closed. Storms tapered off during the late afternoon and early evening period. There were no reports of injuries or fatalities.
episodes.215419: A line of showers and thunderstorms began to form during the late morning and early afternoon hours across Ohio and continued moving eastward throughout the afternoon and evening hours of August 16, 2026. Daytime heating across central Pennsylvania, coupled with ample moisture and shear allowed for strong-to-severe thunderstorms to continue across portions of the Laurel Highlands and into south-central Pennsylvania. Multiple pockets of tree damage were observed across portions of Cambria, Somerset, and Franklin Counties with isolated instances of damage in Blair County.
episodes.215448: Hurricane Lala formed in the central Pacific and approached the islands from southeast. The hurricane passed just south of the Big Island, then moved northwest and passed south of the rest of the Hawaiian islands. Lala brought catastrophic damage to the Big Island of Hawaii in the form of massive flooding and wind damage. Considerable widespread damage due to the winds and flooding was also felt over the rest of the islands.
episodes.215500: During the 16th late afternoon an MCS developed upstream before moving across central Indiana. Moderate instability along with modest enhancement of mid-level flow allowed for the MCS to remain loosely-organized as it pushed through the area. This loosely-organized MCS produced isolated tree and powerline damage and a measured severe wind gust of 60 mph (52 knots).||A measured peak thunderstorm wind gust of 60 mph (52 knots) was recorded near Bartholomew County at 17:16 EST. The storm continued southeastward into Jennings County, where estimated thunderstorm wind gusts of 58 mph (50 knots) occurred around 17:46 EST. The strong wind gusts caused localized utility damage in Jennings County, where a downed tree fell across power lines.
episodes.216062: Scattered convection developed in a strongly unstable environment with MUCAPE values exceeding 3500 J/kg and weak upper flow with increasing DCAPE values around 1000 J/kg through the afternoon.
episodes.216176: An upper level disturbance interacted with an unstable airmass to produce a cluster of severe thunderstorms from Sangamon County eastward through Edgar County during the afternoon of August 16rh.  Wind damage was widespread with the storms.
episodes.216244: Rounds of rain and thunderstorms continued into the middle of August as a front remained in the vicinity on the 15th, lifted north as a warm front on the 16th, and then a cold front passed through on the 17th. ||Some strong to severe thunderstorms were noted during this timeframe, with daily observations of downed trees and power lines in northeast Kentucky from the 15th to the 17th. 72-hour rainfall amounts generally ranged from one to three inches, although some pockets of three to five inches were observed. Seemingly endless rounds of precipitation during the first half of the month had already saturated soils across much of the area. Thus, even lesser rainfall amounts were needed to cause some roadway flooding in northeast Kentucky.
episodes.216245: Rounds of rain and thunderstorms continued into the middle of August as a front remained in the vicinity of southeast Ohio on the 15th, lifted north as a warm front on the 16th, and then a cold front passed through on the 17th. ||Daily showers and thunderstorms that pressed through the area during this time casted swaths of tree and power line damage across southeast Ohio. Additionally, 72-hour rainfall amounts generally ranged from one to three inches, although some pockets of three to five inches were also observed. Seemingly endless rounds of precipitation during the first half of the month had already saturated soils across much of the area. Thus, even lesser rainfall amounts resulted in flooded roads and rises on creeks and streams in southeast Ohio. Impacts from heavier rain also included water rescues, some flooded structures, and river flooding on Duck Creek, Sunday Creek.
episodes.216246: Rounds of rain and thunderstorms continued in West Virginia as a front remained in the vicinity on August 15th, lifted north as a warm front on the 16th, and then a cold front passed through on the 17th. 72-hour rainfall amounts generally ranged from one to three inches, though some pockets of three to five inches were observed. Seemingly endless rounds of precipitation during the first half of the month had already saturated soils across much of the area. Thus, even lesser rainfall amounts resulted in flooded roads across portions of West Virginia. Impacts from heavier rain also included water rescues, flooded structures, and river flooding on Clear Fork, Sand Run, Elk Twomile Creek, Tygart Valley River, West Fork River, and Middle Island Creek. Additionally, episodic rounds of strong thunderstorms produced during this timeframe resulted in more downed trees and power lines across the state. This occurred in locations that had already faced powerful storms earlier in the month, adding to the total of storm damage costs.
episodes.216360: Scattered thunderstorms moved across eastern Colorado. Heavy rain with isolated flash flooding occurred. Flooding appeared to be brief and limited to flowing over roadways. Isolated hail and strong winds reported as well from the thunderstorms.
episodes.216526: A cluster of storms across West Virginia and Virginia spawned isolated to scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms across central North Carolina. The strongest cells produced damaging wind reports across Person, Granville, Orange, Alamance, Guilford, and Davidson Counties.
episodes.217218: Isolated thunderstorms developed during the evening hours in a warm and moist air mass. Some of the storms continued to produce locally heavy rainfall into the overnight hours.
episodes.217435: This event continued the excessively active weather week from August 9th through the 15th. This event the followed the one just just 24 hours earlier, and brought excessive rainfall to Iowa and Illinois, especially south of Interstate 80, where four day rainfall totals of 4 to 10 inches were reported.|This long duration of active weather was supported by a stationary front over the area, with heat, and exceptionally high levels of moisture.  Daily weak disturbances triggered storms.

episodes.217465: In the wake of overnight thunderstorm activity, instability built up during the late morning and early afternoon hours of August 16th, with 1500-2000 J/kg of surface-based CAPE developing. Storm activity renewed by midday in western Ohio, associated with a mesoscale convective vortex. Sufficient deep shear allowed separate storm clusters to consolidate into a larger line that swept across eastern Ohio during the early to mid afternoon hours. The result was widespread reports of wind damage, mainly to trees. One person in Muskingum County was injured by a falling tree. A few isolated instances of flash flooding also occurred due to the multiple storm rounds.
episodes.217466: In the wake of overnight thunderstorm activity, instability built up during the late morning and early afternoon hours of August 16th, with 1500-2000 J/kg of surface-based CAPE developing. Storm activity renewed by midday in Ohio, associated with a mesoscale convective vortex. Sufficient deep shear allowed separate storm clusters to consolidate into a larger line that swept across the region during the afternoon. The result was widespread reports of wind damage, mainly to trees, as well as two QLCS tornadoes embedded in the line.  Additional storm activity behind the main line created some instances of flash flooding near the I-80 corridor.
episodes.217467: In the wake of overnight thunderstorm activity, instability built up during the late morning and early afternoon hours of August 16th, with 1500-2000 J/kg of surface-based CAPE developing. Storm activity renewed by midday in Ohio, associated with a mesoscale convective vortex. Sufficient deep shear allowed separate storm clusters to consolidate into a larger line that swept across the region during the afternoon. The result was widespread reports of wind damage, mainly to trees. Reports of flash flooding were also received from Tucker County.
episodes.217592: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the late morning and early afternoon along a boundary moving through the region.
episodes.217639: Numerous multi-cell thunderstorms developed near a quasi-stationary boundary across central Oklahoma on the afternoon and evening of the 16th. Several areas of thunderstorm wind damage were observed due to downbursts, including on the northeast sides of Norman, OK.
episodes.218076: Large-scale ridging, strong surface heating, deep moisture as well as a moderately unstable airmass supported thunderstorms capable of producing localized heavy rainfall.
episodes.218159: A shortwave moved through the Great Lakes region on the afternoon of August 16th behind a warm front that pass through earlier in the morning. With the warm air advection, instability rose to 1500-2000 J/kg of MLCAPE with a saturated air mass of over 2.0 PWAT. Deep layer shear was also on the lower end at 20-30 knots. An MCV formed in Western Ohio and moved eastward producing scattered damaging wind gusts through North Central Ohio.
episodes.218160: Scattered to widespread thunderstorms formed across the central to western combined OK/TX Panhandles, eventually spreading north. With these storms there were a few isolated severe wind gusts in Hartley and Carson counties in the Texas Panhandle. The gusts measured in Hartley County topped out at 64 mph while one gust in Carson County was measured at 69 mph.
episodes.218239: During the late afternoon and evening hours of August 15th, isolated showers and thunderstorms developed and progressed over north central Kentucky near the Bluegrass region. With afternoon high temperatures in the 90s and dew points in the low-to-mid 70s, this helped produce MLCAPE values up to around 2500-3000 J/kg. While weaker wind shear did limit the extent of convective development, the higher instability and ample moisture in the form of PW greater than 2 did result in isolated thunderstorm wind damage and flash flooding. During the late afternoon through the late evening hours of the 16th, scattered thunderstorms moved over southern Indiana and north central Kentucky ahead of a cold front passing through the Ohio Valley. While there was meager deep-layer shear in place, a 30-40 kt LLJ, ample instability of MLCAPE around 2500-3000 J/kg, and decent moisture with PW over 1.8 helped result in some thunderstorms producing severe wind gusts and damage.
episodes.218241: During the late afternoon through the late evening hours of the 16th, scattered thunderstorms moved over southern Indiana and north central Kentucky ahead of a cold front passing through the Ohio Valley. While there was meager deep-layer shear in place, a 30-40 kt LLJ, ample instability of MLCAPE around 2500-3000 J/kg, and decent moisture with PW over 1.8 helped result in some thunderstorms producing severe wind gusts and damage.

episodes.218360: An upper low was located just southeast of El Paso while southeast flow at the surface brought in some modest monsoonal moisture.  A thunderstorm stalled out near Loop 375 and Montana which brought flash flooding to the area.
episodes.218362: A weak upper low remained just southeast of El Paso and combined with some good monsoonal surface moisture to bring another round of slow moving storms to east El Paso. Flash flooding near the intersection of Montana and Tierra Este was reported for the second day in a row.
episodes.218390: Isolated thunderstorms moved across northwest North Carolina during the afternoon. One of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts in Iredell County.
episodes.218525: Isolated thunderstorms during the afternoon and transitioned to clusters of thunderstorms across far western Kansas into the evening in an unstable airmass. Several reports of severe wind and hail occurred with these thunderstorms.
episodes.218594: An isolated waterspout was observed in association with a lee convergence convective line extending northwest of the Lower Florida Keys.  A Saharan Air Layer airmass was beginning to move over the Florida Keys coastal waters.

This tornado was confirmed based on video evidence, a storm damage survey, and satellite imagery of crop damage. The tornado began just northeast of the intersection of State Route 235 and Apple Road. The tornado then moved east-northeast across open fields, crossing Mount Pleasant Cemetery Road.||Most of the damage from the tornado occurred near the intersection of Ward Road and Kiser Lake Road. Several trees were downed at this intersection, as well as slightly to the east on Ward Road. A home on Ward Road had some of its siding removed. Elk Twomile Creek at Charleston exceeded a bankfull level of 6.5 feet on the afternoon of August 16th. The creek briefly dipped below bankfull during the evening, then rose back above bankfull to a crest around 9.3 feet when a secondary round of heavy rainfall passed overhead. The creek returned to its banks during the night. Flooding occurred along Greenbrier Street and Rutledge Road while the creek was out of its banks.
